oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache prefill rate spike detected in us-west-2 serving pool. 95th mem growth 18% in last 3m. Prefill_count/sec up 7x. Triggering autoscale thrash.

maria: seeing the same. tail latenc y for text-gen routes up ~400ms -> 1.4s at p95. any recent rollout that touched batching/prefill?

raj: rolled a config to increase continuous_batch_window from 30ms -> 60ms two hours ago for canary. Not global yet, but the canary had 40% traffic. Could be warmup behavior.

sre-jen: logs show a small blob of clients sending many short prompts that cause prefix inflation. kvcache:key_count per pod jumped from 200k -> 1.1M in ~4m. evictions also spike. this is classic staircase prefill.

maria: immediate steps: 1) throttle prefill on canary pods 2) reduce continuous_batch_window 3) temporarily increase HPA min replicas to stabilize. I'll patch canary now.

maria: patching canary env -> set KVCACHE_PREFILL_LIMIT=200
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-canary KVCACHE_PREFILL_LIMIT=200
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-canary CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20
```

infra-bot: deploy rolling-update started for deployment/redwood-canary (maria) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

raj: I've paused the config rollout in the console. Stopping further traffic to canary.

sre-jen: metrics after ~90s: prefill_count/sec on canary down 85%, mem growth stabilized. p95 latency trending down ~300ms improvement. autoscaler still sees queue depth spikes from warmup across pool.

maria: scaling HPA for the serving pool to add 3 replicas to soak the current queues.
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy redwood-serving --replicas=12
```

infra-bot: HPA manual scale accepted; new desired replicas: 12

cs-lina: heads up — CS ticket #4237 from BigRetail reported degraded response times just now. They were seeing ~2s slower responses but no errors. I've notified them mitigation is in progress.

maria: good. short customer impact: degraded latency for a small % of calls (retail checkout flows), no request loss. We'll update SLA if this persists.

dev-platform-lee: quick thought — could enable prefix-dedup as a guard. It might reduce prefill amplification for repeated cold prefixes. We can toggle on the canary.

raj: enabling prefix-dedup on canary now (env PREFIX_DEDUP=true)
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-canary PREFIX_DEDUP=true
```

sre-jen: after prefix-dedup toggle and prefill_limit, memory per pod dropped ~22% within 3m. tail latency back near baseline. autoscaler stopped oscillating.

maria: triage notes for handoff:
- root cause hypothesis: canary config increase of continuous_batch_window created longer batching windows causing more aggressive prefill of KV cache for many short prompts -> key explosion -> eviction churn -> HPA queue depth thrash
- mitigations applied: set KVCACHE_PREFILL_LIMIT=200, set CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20 on canary, enabled PREFIX_DEDUP, manual scale to 12 replicas
- customer impact: CS ticket #4237; p95 latency transient +1.5s for small subset, no 5xx; monitoring ticket created
- followups: run replay of short-prompt workload against canary config, add canary safety gate (prefill_limit <= 500), add HPA hysteresis (min-stabilize 180s) and a warmup smoothing policy

maria: tagging @raj @dev-platform-lee for postmortem. I'm going offline in 10m — handing off to @sre-jen for next 4h.

raj: ack. I'll coordinate a quick postmortem doc and include the replay test.

sre-jen: taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 2h then escalate if anything recurs. Handoff summary pinned to thread. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident closed in thread: mitigation applied, metrics stable for 12m. Please file a postmortem if you changed control plane configs.
